label: PF Backlog 580
title: Eventing SSOT (Go): transports - inproc callbacks, webhook (HMAC+idempotency), notify/email
body:
## Problem / why
Push transport only exists in the frozen dashboard websocket; external delivery and email are bespoke.

## Goal / value
Pluggable transports behind one interface: inproc (callbacks), webhook (HTTP POST, HMAC signature,
idempotency key), notify/email (reuse notification_system + alerts).

## In scope
- inproc transport (compat with event_bus.on); webhook transport (signing + retry); notify/email adapter.

## Out of scope
- SSE (API surface, E9); alert routing (E6).

## Acceptance criteria
- A subscriber receives via each transport; webhook verifies HMAC; email respects priority gate.

## Verification / test plan
- Webhook HMAC test; inproc callback test; email adapter test.

## Dependencies & links
- E2 (webhook contract), E4 (dispatcher).

objective:
Pluggable transports behind one interface: inproc (callbacks), webhook (HTTP POST, HMAC signature,
idempotency key), notify/email (reuse notification_system + alerts).
acceptance_criteria: A subscriber receives events through inproc, webhook and notify/email transports with dispatcher-owned retry/DLQ.
Webhook requests carry timestamp+body HMAC, event_id idempotency key, reject invalid signatures, and classify 4xx/409/429/5xx correctly.
Notify always stores in-app notifications and sends email only for eligible priorities when SMTP is configured; missing SMTP does not fail in-app delivery.
Transports enforce target/security policy, use one registry, emit observability, and are covered by unit plus dispatcher integration tests.

evidence:
Gate 1.5 architect review - model=mimo-v2.6-flash sha=ac0af4157448
BLOCKER:
  - CL-015 unmet: every `ac_evidence`/`coverage`/`traceability` entry cites `docs/EVENT-TRANSPORTS-DESIDE.md` with no candidate SHA; design doc is used as its own proof, so AC evidence is unverifiable.
  - Language rule risk: `api_contract` artifact is `api/routers/events.py` for a new `POST /api/v1/notifications` endpoint; new shipped logic must be Go unless this is explicitly an edit to a shipped Python route (not stated).
  - CL-011/checklist-3 unmet: all five implementation controls record `tenant_test: N/A: transport receives tenant-scoped subscription` — no proof of boundary authz, tenant binding, or NOSUPERUSER/NOBYPASSRLS posture for the transport/registry path.
  - CL-013 not pinned: webhook HMAC verification does not specify constant-time comparison, nor per-subscription/tenant key binding (single `PF_WEBHOOK_HMAC_KEY` implies a shared secret).
MAJOR:
  - Checklist 8 incomplete: `needs_api` is implied but only `route` is given; method, authn, authz, validation, and tenant-scoping for `POST /api/v1/notifications` are undefined, so the API contract cannot be kept in sync.
  - Contracts out of sync: functional_spec declares `PF_SMTP_*` while design_pack config lists `PF_WEBHOOK_HMAC_KEY, PF_NOTIFY_*`; email-threshold and SMTP keys are not reconciled to one config contract.
  - Checklist 1/6 incomplete: rollback is "remove transports/endpoint" with no handling of stranded DLQ entries, in-flight retries, or subscriptions referencing a removed transport; no verified backup/restore path stated.
  - Checklist 2 unaddressed: no on-startup defence-in-depth check, no statement of behaviour when dispatcher/worker/DB is down, and no alert lead-time for DLQ growth.
  - Checklist 10 under-specified: observability is only the phrase "delivery metrics/logs" — no named metrics, DLQ-depth signal, or redaction rule for secrets/targets in logs.
  - Failure classification incomplete relative to AC-2: `429` (and `Retry-After`) handling is absent from the failure matrix, and the "4xx permanent except 401/403 bounded retry" decision conflicts with "permanent 4xx → DLQ".
MINOR:
  - Checklist 5: ordering/dedup invariant across transports is unstated — only `event_id` idempotency is given; no cross-transport duplicate-delivery rule or sequence/ordering test.
  - Checklist 9: retention/redaction for webhook target URLs, HMAC keys, and DLQ payloads is not specified beyond "no secret logging".
  - AC-1 evidence lists only `go test ./... and API tests` with no dispatcher-integration test named for the notify path (C-3's negative test reuses `notify_test.go`).
  - Config surface lacks a documented precedence/default for `PF_NOTIFY_EMAIL_MIN_PRIORITY` when unset (fail-open vs fail-closed).
NIT:
  - `traceability.test` and `test_matrix.test` use globs (`go/eventtransport/*_test.go`) rather than concrete test files, weakening Gate-2 pinning.
  - `stop_conditions: ['SSE requested']` is a scope guard, not a delivery stop condition.
  - `affected_components` / `affected_files` / `risks` in Gate-1 context are "Not specified", leaving the blast-radius review without declared files.
SUMMARY:
  - Direction is sound (single Transport interface, dispatcher-owned retry/DLQ, reuse of notification_system), but the design is not Gate-1.5-ready: evidence lacks candidate SHAs (CL-015), tenant/RLS posture is explicitly N/A'd (CL-011), and constant-time HMAC/tenant key binding is unpinned (CL-013).
  - Top risks before proceeding: undefined API contract for the new notifications endpoint, unreconciled config contracts, and rollback that strands DLQ/in-flight events.
  - Recommend returning to Gate 1 to close BLOCKERs and the API/config/rollback MAJORs; do not advance to coding until dispositions are recorded per CL-006.
RECOMMENDATION: BLOCKED - objectively verifiable blocker(s) present

requirements.title: In-process and webhook transports
requirements.preconditions: Dispatcher and event store are live.
acceptance: Given a subscriber, when dispatched via inproc or webhook, then delivery is attempted and failures follow dispatcher retry/DLQ.

requirements.title: Notify/email transport and API
requirements.preconditions: Dispatcher and event store are live.
acceptance: Given a notify event, when delivered, then in-app is stored and email follows the priority gate.

requirements.title: Permanent failure classification
requirements.preconditions: Dispatcher and event store are live.
acceptance: Given a permanent webhook failure, when dispatched, then it goes to DLQ without retry.

requirements.title: Security and observability
requirements.preconditions: Dispatcher and event store are live.
acceptance: Given a target or HMAC key, when validated, then SSRF/secret rules apply and signals are emitted.

functional_spec.data_lifecycle: in-app notifications retained by existing store
open_questions: SMTP deployment values are supplied by environment.
dod: Delivery Complete requires all five states

design_pack.security: Per-subscription HMAC key via auth_ref; constant-time hmac.Equal; timestamp+body; 5-minute skew; SSRF blocks; secrets never logged; tenant from subscription; runtime roles NOSUPERUSER/NOBYPASSRLS where DB-backed.
design_pack.observability: event_delivery_attempts_total, event_delivery_retry_age_seconds, event_delivery_dlq_depth, event_delivery_latency_seconds; redact targets/keys/signatures.
design_pack.rollback: Remove transports/endpoint; disable subscriptions using removed transports; retain delivery/DLQ history; verified backup before destructive cleanup; no migration.

implementation_controls.control: inproc callbacks and webhook delivery share one Transport contract
webhook HMAC timestamp+body and idempotency key
notify stores in-app and gates email by priority
permanent webhook errors bypass retry and go to DLQ
transport failures and deliveries emit metrics/logs
transport registry rejects cross-tenant subscription lookup
